transcript.text: dishwaher leakin water all over the floor and the plug sockets are right next to it whats going on

Water near the plug or socket is dangerous. Please don't touch the plug, socket or machine if they or your hands are wet. If you can do it safely, switch off the circuit at the consumer unit (fuse box), keep away from the water, and don't use the machine again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has checked it. Water leaking near live sockets is a serious electrical hazard, so please do not use the appliance until a qualified engineer has checked it. This could be caused by a split door seal, a blocked filter, or a loose hose connection allowing water to escape onto the floor. With the machine switched off and unplugged, you can safely check if anything is caught on the rubber door seal or if tall items are deflecting spray out of the door. Please let me know what you find with those checks so I can advise further.
its still running tho!! theres loads of bubbles coming out the bottom of the door and the water is spreading toward an extension lead on the floor. should i just turn it off at the wall?

Yes, switch it off at the wall immediately to stop the water and eliminate the electrical hazard near the extension lead. Please keep away from any standing water or sockets until a qualified engineer has checked it. The bubbles suggest excess foam, often caused by too much detergent or the wrong type, which can push water out of the door seal. Once safe, you might check if the door seal is blocked by debris, but do not attempt to use the machine again until it has been professionally inspected.
